definitions.explanation: A person who wishes or hopes to do something; someone who has applied or expressed interest.

examples.japanese: {希望者|きぼうしゃ}は{受付|うけつけ}で{申|もう}し{込|こ}んでください。
examples.english: Those who are interested, please register at the reception.

examples.japanese: {参加|さんか}{希望者|きぼうしゃ}が{多|おお}かった。
examples.english: There were many people who wanted to participate.

examples.japanese: {希望者|きぼうしゃ}{全員|ぜんいん}に{資料|しりょう}を{配|くば}った。
examples.english: We distributed materials to all applicants.

notes:
{希望者|きぼうしゃ} combines {希望|きぼう} (hope, wish) + {者|しゃ} (person).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～{希望者|きぼうしゃ} (people who want to ~)
- {希望者|きぼうしゃ}は... (those who are interested...)
- {希望者|きぼうしゃ}{多数|たすう} (many applicants)

RELATED -者 COMPOUNDS:
- {参加者|さんかしゃ} (participant)
- {利用者|りようしゃ} (user)
- {志願者|しがんしゃ} (volunteer, applicant)
- {応募者|おうぼしゃ} (applicant)

USAGE NOTES:
- Often used in announcements and official contexts
- The ～{者|しゃ} suffix creates agent nouns from verb stems or nouns
